text:
elena: Heads-up: we flipped the int2-fast profile on onboarding-candidate for a short throughput test. Tokens/sec looks great but rerank and paraphrase slices show big quality churn. failing ids: s3://redwood-curation/onboard/rerank/fails-6930011111.txt :worried:

pat: Yikes. Any quick metric? identical_prefix_6 or kv_prefix_dup_frac?

elena: added identical_first_6_tokens = 0.34 (baseline 0.04), kv_prefix_dup_frac = 0.28. Seems many different prompts collapse to same early token sequence post-quant.

maurice: Could this be pad-token remapping in the int2 kernel? We had a recent opt that remaps rare-token encodings to save bits. If two different rare subwords alias to same compressed code, early-token collisions make sense.

anya: Good theory. Try FP16 fallback and also run a small hash-regeneration check: sometimes tokenizer hash table regen changed bucket boundaries. Elena: do we have the build hash for tokenizer in the binary?

elena: Model binary tokenizer hash = tokhash-2026-03-10-a9. Eval runner uses tokhash-2026-03-10-a9 as well. Running fp16 fallback with kv debug now: 
```
./eval_run --model onboarding-candidate:int2-fast --prompts s3://redwood-curation/onboard/rerank/manifest.json \
  --kv-debug --fallback fp16 --out ./runs/onboard-int2-fp16-6930011111.json
```

labelops_bot: Label queue created: queue_id=lab-q-2026-03-30-21, size=520, sampler=onboard-dedupe-0.85, priority=high

maurice: Also run a quick token-hash-regeneration diff on the manifest to verify there wasn't a subtle ingest transform: 
```
python tools/tokenhash_diff.py --manifest s3://redwood-curation/onboard/rerank/manifest.json \
  --tokhash tokhash-2026-03-10-a9 --out /tmp/tokdiff-6930011111.txt
```

pat: If fp16 restores quality that's a strong indicator kernel compression/aliasing is the cause. If so runtime may need to disable remap or adjust mapping table. If not, dataset dupes might be the issue.

elena: FP16 run completed. Paraphrase/rerank metrics restored within 2% of baseline. FP16 traces uploaded: s3://redwood-runs/onboard/int2-fp16-6930011111.json. KV traces show collisions only on int2 run.

runtime-ci: We have a canary kernel option `--no-rare-remap` that disables rare-token remapping. Recommend running int2 canary with that flag to confirm. We can spin a canary in a 1hr window.

maurice: If canary matches FP16, plan: patch kernel to disable remap by default for int2 and add synthetic anchors that exercise rare subword pairs. Also run a micro-label pass for dedupe-reduced anchors.

labelops_bot: Queue update: shard1=130 assigned, shard2=130 queued, shard3=130 queued, shard4=130 queued. Progress URL: https://labels.redwood/queues/lab-q-2026-03-30-21

anya: Parallel: @maurice please generate 150 synthetics targeting rare-subword collisions (swap, splice ops on low-freq tokens) and stage to s3://redwood-curation/onboard/rerank/synthetics/rare-subword-150.json. Reserve 100 golden review slots.

maurice: Will run: `python tools/synth_rare_subword.py --src s3://redwood-curation/onboard/rerank/golden.json --out s3://redwood-curation/onboard/rerank/synthetics/rare-subword-150.json --n 150 --ops swap,splice`

runtime-ci: Canary run with `--no-rare-remap` scheduled now. If results align with fp16 we'll file RUNTIME-1152 to revert the remap. If not, continue relabel + augment.

elena: Canary matched FP16. Rerank and paraphrase restored. Upload: s3://redwood-runs/onboard/int2-canary-6930011111.json. Locking auto-rollout of int2-fast profile until RUNTIME-1152 lands and we finish the lab relabel pass.

pat: Good outcome. Maurice, after you push synthetics, please also add a small monitoring probe in the console: `frac_rare_subword_collision` so future regressions show up quickly.

maurice: On it. I'll also add a daily alert if `frac_rare_subword_collision > 0.05` for any int profile.

anya: Thanks team. Next check-in after first shard finishes or when RUNTIME-1152 is merged.
